releases.name: v0.3.0 - two-layer routing with Otari policies and Otari-Tags
releases.body:
## Two-layer routing

Magpie picks the intent tier; Otari picks the real provider, enforces budget, and handles failover.

### Added

- Otari routing policies are exposed as Magpie models by policy name (`otari/fast`, `otari/strong`, `otari/long`).
- `Otari-Tags` on every request: `app=magpie,session=<id>,model=<id>`, so usage can be filtered per conversation.
- `npm run setup:routing` creates `fast` / `strong` / `long` Otari policies with provider failover.
- `docs/two-layer-routing.md` with the full setup, verification and demo script.

### Fixed

- Organization provider-key models now use the callable selector (`<key-prefix>:<model>`) instead of a native id Otari does not accept.
- Policy models send the bare policy name, matching Otari's model spelling.

### Verified

- `magpie provider test otari` -> `chat 592 ms - fast`
- Local gateway: a quick question routes to `otari/fast`; a test-writing prompt routes to `otari/strong`.
- 41 unit tests pass.

### Upstream feedback

- https://github.com/mozilla-ai/otari/issues/3017
- https://github.com/mozilla-ai/otari/issues/3018

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/kabaBZ/magpie-otari-provider/compare/v0.2.1...v0.3.0

releases.name: v0.2.1 — organization provider labels actually work
releases.body:
Fixes the organization-provider label introduced in v0.2.0.

## Fixed
- The plain `GET /api/v1/models` listing reports every model as
  `pricing_source: "configured"`. Otari only marks a model
  `pricing_source: "organization"` when the listing is asked for one
  organization provider key by name (`?provider=<key>`).
- The plugin now reads `GET /organizations/me/provider-keys`, then asks
  `GET /models?provider=<key>` for each usable key, and overlays those rows
  onto the catalog list. No key name is hard-coded.
- Models served by your own key now show the key name, e.g.
  `[mydeepseek] deepseek/deepseek-flash`.

## Notes
- Falls back to the organization name, then the provider name, when a
  key listing cannot be read.
- Model discovery still works when the Dashboard session has expired;
  the prefix is simply not added.

## Install
```bash
magpie plugin add npm:magpie-otari-provider
```

releases.name: v0.2.0 — label models served by your own provider keys
releases.body:
Models served by provider keys your organization added under **Organization → Providers** are now labelled, so they can be told apart from deployment-hosted ones.

## Added
- `pricing_source: "organization"` models carry an `organizationOwned` flag.
- Display name is prefixed in this order:
  1. the provider key name (`[mydeepseek]`), when the Dashboard session can read it and it is unambiguous for that provider;
  2. the organization name (`[kaba's organization]`);
  3. `[organization Inference providers: <provider>]`;
  4. `[organization Inference providers]` when the provider is unknown.

The prefix is display-only: model IDs and requests are unchanged.

## Notes
- The label needs a Dashboard session for the key and organization names. Without one it falls back to the provider name, and model discovery still works.

## Install
```bash
magpie plugin add magpie-otari-provider
```

releases.name: v0.1.1 — publishable package fix
releases.body:
Fixes a release-blocking bug in v0.1.0.

## Fixed
- Removed a self-referential `file:.pkgtest/...` entry from `dependencies`.
  v0.1.0 failed to install for every user because npm tried to unpack
  that local tarball. v0.1.1 has no runtime dependencies at all.

## Install
```bash
magpie plugin add magpie-otari-provider
```

releases.name: v0.1.0 — Otari provider for Magpie
releases.body:
First release of the Otari provider plugin for Magpie.

## Features
- Dynamic Chat model discovery from `GET /api/v1/models` (145 models on the hosted gateway).
- Per-million-token pricing, with `/pricing/current` as a fallback.
- Dashboard session login by cookie or email/password, plus API-key-only mode.
- Balance, key budget, reset time, 30-day usage and routing visibility.
- OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, streaming and non-streaming.

## Install
```bash
magpie plugin add magpie-otari-provider
```

## Notes
- `free` is only set when Otari states a per-token input and output price of zero.
- Tiered prices show the base tier; a long-context request can cost more.
